newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas slips late, longs bail before expiry.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas slips late, longs bail before expiry.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, after a record run up early Thursday, reversed course late, as longs opted to take profits and liquidate ahead of the spot-December expiry later today, sources said.

December, which rallied 22.3 cents early to an all-time spot high of $3.85 per million British thermal units, retreated to $3.38 by 1400 EST. January was 16.4 cents lower at $3.10 after earlier setting a new benchmark of $3.45.
"It's looking a little soft right now and we could see more downside as longs get out," said a Houston trader, adding cash firmed again today on the cold weather.

While the market was technically overbought and due for a profit taking pullback after a 46 percent surge in six sessions, few expected prices to collapse with well-below normal temperatures expected to blanket the nation for the rest of the month.
Most agreed cold weather and relatively low storage in some regions made it likely December Gulf Coast indices would be well over $3 when bidweek draws to a close early next week.

AGA data Wednesday showed U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 86 bcf. Overall inventories were still 181 bcf, or six percent, below year-ago, and Producing Region storage was at 69 percent full, well under last year's levels.

Chartists noted a lower close today after the early rally to new highs could set up a possible key reversal. They pegged January support at today's low of $3.04, with psychological buying likely at $3. Resistance was seen at today's new contract high of $3.45.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices jumped almost 30 cents Thursday to the mid-$3.60s. Midwest pipes were talked more than 40 cents higher in the mid-to-high $3.60s. New York city gate swing gas was pegged in a wide range from the $4.30s to $4.60s, up more than 30 cents on the day. December gas in New York was quoted in the $5.00 area.
NYMEX said 41,496 Hub contracts traded at 1305 EST. Hub open interest on Nov 20 fell 9,016 contracts to 153,422.

NYMEX December Alberta natgas slipped five cents to $1.85 after setting a new high of $2.03 early. January was up five cents at a new high of $2.05. NYMEX said eight Alberta contracts traded at 1305 EST. Alberta open interest on Nov 20 fell 14 lots to 490.

NYMEX December Permian natgas tumbled 12 cents to $3.33 after rallying to a new benchmark early of $3.50. Deferred months were untraded at 1345 EST. Permian open interest on Nov 20 was unchanged at 466.
NYMEX December Alberta and Permian natgas futures expire Monday, November 25.

On the KCBT, December, which surged 37.8 cents early to a new high of $4.00, slumped to $3.40. Deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread was still at two cents (KCBT premium) versus a NYMEX edge of one-half cent after yesterday's close.
KCBT December natgas expires Friday, November 22.
